description: A responsive structure spec is valid when all three breakpoint tiers are covered, hidden content has a disclosure mechanism, navigation modes are declared per breakpoint, no two breakpoints share the same minWidth, collapsible regions are fully defined, and breakpoints are sorted ascending.

rules.description: responsive-spec.json must exist with breakpoints array, each having name, minWidth, and layout. A responsive spec without breakpoints cannot be validated.
The breakpoints array must include at least one breakpoint named 'mobile' and one named 'desktop'. These are the minimum tiers for a responsive implementation.
Unless mobileOnly:true or desktopOnly:true, the spec must cover mobile (<=480), tablet (481-1023), and desktop (>=1024). Missing a tier leaves users on that device size without a defined layout.
Any region hidden at a breakpoint must declare a disclosureTarget or hiddenIntentional:true. Hiding navigation or key content without a disclosure mechanism creates dead UX.
When navigation is declared, every breakpoint must specify a navMode from the allowed set. Navigation without a mode creates undefined rendering across device sizes.
No two breakpoints may share the same minWidth. Duplicate breakpoint boundaries cause unpredictable CSS media query resolution.
Every entry in collapsibleRegions must declare collapsedAt (array of breakpoint names) and collapseType. Collapsible regions without a collapse definition cannot be implemented.
Breakpoints must be ordered by minWidth from smallest to largest. Out-of-order breakpoints cause CSS specificity issues and make specs harder to reason about.
All breakpoint names must be unique. Duplicate names cause ambiguous references in collapsedAt arrays and navigation breakpoint maps.
